html:
The Buruna, also written Purduna or Burduna, are an Aboriginal people of the dry coastal plains of Western Australia between the Ashburton and Gascoyne rivers, south of present day Onslow.

Their language belongs to the small Kanyara group of Pama-Nyungan languages. Neighbours on the map were the Thalanyji to the north, the Payungu to the west and the Jiwarli inland. Pastoral stations took over the region from the 1870s. Only a little of the language was recorded before it went out of daily use. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Buruna, also written Purduna or Burduna, are an Aboriginal people of the dry coastal plains of Western Australia between the Ashburton and Gascoyne rivers, south of present day Onslow.
